title: Vocal Cleanup and Processing for '...but, I believe in the best part of everything.'
goal: Edit, clean, treat, and mix the multi-layered vocal arrangement for …but, I believe in the best part of everything., using AI to help identify an efficient workflow, solve specific audio problems, and determine appropriate processing and mixing strategies for the different vocal parts.
context:
I am producing a track titled …but, I believe in the best part of everything. that includes a four-part vocal arrangement with multiple vocal octaves and layers. Because the arrangement contains overlapping vocal parts, the individual recordings need to be cleaned, edited, treated, and balanced so that the harmony remains clear without overwhelming the rest of the production.

For this session, I will use AI to assist me in developing and refining a workflow for editing and mixing these vocals. I will work primarily in Ableton Live, using iZotope RX for detailed audio repair and cleanup as necessary. I have professional experience with audio editing, production, and mixing, so I will use my own critical listening and judgment to evaluate the AI's recommendations and adjust them when necessary.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: I did sort of accomplish what I set out for, but honestly found the information propagated a little more slowly than anticipated. I may have had more success doing what I know would work first and then asking questions based off of that.

Step 1.step_name: Assess the Vocal Arrangement and Develop an Editing Strategy
Step 1.step_action: I will describe the vocal arrangement, recording setup, number and ranges of the vocal parts, and any problems I hear in the raw recordings. I will use AI to help determine an efficient order of operations for editing and processing the vocals before beginning detailed work.

nodes.label: Plays back raw vocal and states cleanup goal
nodes.detail: With the raw lead vocal already loaded in the 'bassoon 8-14-26 - VOX' Ableton Live project, the participant plays back a phrase of the raw take and states his goal out loud: clean up the vocals so they sound 'as profound as possible.' He immediately flags pitch and volume inconsistencies by ear.

nodes.label: Opens Claude chat and describes the cleanup task and available tools
nodes.detail: Switches to a Safari tab with a Claude.ai chat titled 'Professional vocal audio cleanup and editing' and explains the vocals have breath noises, pitch issues, and volume inconsistency.

nodes.label: Proposes a general vocal workflow and a tool-specific routing plan
nodes.detail: Claude first lays out the standard order of operations for rough-to-release vocals (repair, pitch, level consistency, EQ, de-essing, glue, space), stressing that order matters more than any single step and warning against over-correcting pitch.

nodes.label: Respond to Claude with the current vocal production setup
nodes.detail: When Claude asks for his setup, he lists Ableton as his DAW, Melodyne for pitch/vocal treatment, iZotope RX for cleanup, and a variety of UAD plugins for shaping the sound.

nodes.label: Generate a tool-specific vocal production plan
nodes.detail: Once told the specific toolset, Claude routes each stage through the participant's actual gear: RX plugins (De-click/De-hum/Voice De-noise) directly on the track, Melodyne via ARA for pitch, clip gain then UAD LA-2A/1176 for level and punch, UAD Neve 1073/Pultec EQP-1A/Manley Massive Passive for EQ, and Studer A800/Ampex tape for warmth, with RX and Melodyne fixes kept before the UAD chain.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about the new plan

Step 2.step_name: Clean and Edit the Individual Vocal Recordings
Step 2.step_action: I will edit the individual vocal tracks and use RX where necessary to address unwanted noises, breaths, clicks, mouth sounds, background noise, or other recording artifacts. I will consult AI about specific problems as they arise and evaluate its suggested RX tools, settings, and editing techniques.

nodes.label: Moves to the verse-2 vocal comp for cleanup
nodes.detail: Transitions to the second vocal part (verse-2 comp), noting out loud that it's an important pass he hasn't done yet.

nodes.label: Runs the RX De-click/De-hum/Voice De-noise chain on verse 2
nodes.detail: Runs essentially the same RX cleanup chain used on verse 1 -- De-click, De-hum, and Voice De-noise -- on this new take, remarking that this recording has a more noticeably inconsistent mic technique/proximity than the first ('inconsistent approach to the microphone, that's pretty obvious').
nodes.softwares: iZotope RX (De-click, De-hum, De-noise, in Ableton)

nodes.label: Catches and corrects an over-aggressive denoise pass
nodes.detail: Auditions the vocal after each RX module and catches that a denoise pass reduced too aggressively at one point, pulling the setting back before continuing.

nodes.label: Bounces the cleaned verse-2 track and troubleshoots a playback artifact
nodes.detail: Bounces/places the cleaned verse-2 track when satisfied, briefly troubleshooting an unexpected distortion artifact on playback before moving on to processing.

Step 3.step_action: I will process the cleaned vocal tracks using EQ, compression, de-essing, saturation, and other processing where appropriate. I will use AI to help troubleshoot specific sonic problems and suggest processing approaches that create a consistent vocal sound while accounting for differences between vocal registers, performances, and layers.

nodes.label: Runs Melodyne pitch correction on the verse-2 vocal
nodes.detail: Opens Melodyne on 'Main Vox V1' (verse 2) and runs the same quantize/correct-pitch macro workflow used on verse 1.

nodes.label: Manually nudges mis-detected notes in the lower range
nodes.detail: Manually nudges notes that Melodyne mis-detects, particularly in the lower part of his range, where he says the software 'gets weird ideas of what the pitch is.'

nodes.label: Compares verse-2 pitch passes against the finished verse-1 vocal
nodes.detail: Listens back to multiple passes of the phrase ('You say you can't believe, sang the saddest song you knew...'), pulling automation/corrections back when he doesn't trust an aggressive correction, and comparing the result against the already-finished verse-1 vocal for consistency.

nodes.label: Judges the vocal 'a little dead' and asks Claude what to try
nodes.detail: Once pitch-corrected, judges the verse-2 vocal 'a little dead' and asks Claude what to try, explaining he's redoing this vocal because a previous treatment didn't sit right in the mix.

nodes.label: Diagnoses over-de-brightening and suggests fixes for sparkle
nodes.detail: Explains the 'dead' feeling is common after a de-brightening EQ pass and suggests several targeted fixes: turning the Little Plate Mod switch back on for reverb-tail shimmer, a broad Pultec-style high shelf (10-16kHz) instead of a narrow boost, driving tape saturation slightly harder, checking whether the de-esser is over-triggering, and shortening reverb pre-delay.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response and ask about tape saturation
nodes.detail: The participant reviews Claude's response about over-brightening and suggested fixes for sparkle, then asks which tape saturation plugin to use from the available options, including Saturn, Softube, Decapitator, and UAD tape plugins.

nodes.label: Recommends Saturn multiband plus one full-band tape sim
nodes.detail: Clarifies Decapitator is meant for adding grit/character rather than gentle cleanup, and recommends FabFilter Saturn multiband applied only to a high band (~3-4kHz and up) for surgical sparkle without touching the protected low-mids, plus a single full-band UAD Studer A800 or Ampex tape emulation underneath for overall glue, explicitly advising against also stacking Softube or Decapitator for this pass.

nodes.label: Review and apply Claude's Saturn and tape saturation recommendation
nodes.detail: The participant reviews Claude's recommendation to use Saturn multiband on the high band together with a full-band tape saturation plugin, applies the combination, and is satisfied with the resulting brighter, more saturated vocal character.
nodes.softwares: Claude chat (Safari), Ableton Live (FabFilter Saturn, UAD tape saturation)

nodes.label: Asks Claude for final finishing-touch ideas
nodes.detail: Asks Claude 'any last minute ideas to really put it over the top?' looking for finishing touches beyond the core processing chain.

nodes.label: Suggests parallel compression, delay throws, and automation polish
nodes.detail: Suggests parallel (New York) compression on a heavily squashed bus blended underneath the main vocal, short delay throws automated only at phrase endings, cautious/subtle doubling to avoid thinning the low voice, a manual automation pass to emphasize emotionally key words, automating effect sends rather than leaving them static, and checking mono compatibility of the reverb/delay returns.

nodes.label: Test an additional processing option in Ableton Live
nodes.detail: The participant reviews Claude's suggestions for parallel compression, delay throws, and automation polish, then tests an additional processing option in Ableton Live and decides the existing vocal already sounds good without needing the added processing.

nodes.label: Asks Claude about referencing the mix through SoundID Reference
nodes.detail: Asks 'Should I try it with sound ID' referring to SoundID Reference, an app he owns that emulates different listening environments (car, AirPods, flat/'War Flat' monitoring).

nodes.label: Explains SoundID's role and warns against baking it into the bounce
nodes.detail: Explains SoundID Reference calibrates monitors/headphones to a flat response so EQ/compression judgments aren't fooled by room or speaker coloration, but stresses it must stay on the monitoring/master bus only and never be printed into the actual mix bounce, since it corrects what he hears, not what he prints.

nodes.label: Review Claude's SoundID guidance and agree to use his ear
nodes.detail: The participant reviews Claude's explanation of SoundID's role and agrees that using his ear to judge the vocal is the right choice.

nodes.label: Freezes the verse-2 vocal and checks whether the hour is up
nodes.detail: Freezes/flattens the verse-2 vocal (bounce in place) and asks aloud whether roughly an hour has elapsed, wrapping up the processing pass.

nodes.label: Browses bounced vocal files in Finder
nodes.detail: After confirming roughly an hour has elapsed, opens a Finder window titled 'Consolidate' to show the bounced/consolidated vocal audio files produced during the session, browsing filenames and timestamps of the exported takes.

nodes.label: Troubleshoots an unexpected Ableton playback glitch
nodes.detail: Back in Ableton, runs into an unexplained issue where audio starts playing that he didn't expect, saying 'what is happening, how is anything starting after that, there shouldn't be anything recording,' and after more confused troubleshooting, 'I have no idea what's happening.'

nodes.label: Suggests sending the vocal to Claude instead of continuing live troubleshooting
nodes.detail: For the sake of time, suggests he could just send the vocal itself to Claude rather than continue troubleshooting live; the recording ends mid-sentence.

ratings.output_quality_reason: It met most of the five rubric requirements, but I didn’t get far enough to test the 4 part. It usually is a little quicker of a process.
